source: Townsville City Plan, Schedule 7 - Places of cultural heritage value, Version 2025/01, Table SC7.1.1
purpose: Townsville does not publish its Heritage overlay (or the Pre-1911 building overlay) as a queryable ArcGIS feature service (only Bushfire/zoning/sewer/water are queryable - see poc/site_layers.json and poc/zoning_layers.json TOWNSVILLE notes). Schedule 7 is a CURRENT (not superseded) scheme table that lists every local- and state-listed heritage place by lot/plan, street address and place name, giving a usable text-schedule alternative to a missing overlay layer - same technique as Livingstone Schedule 3 and Burke Schedule 5.
extraction_method: PyMuPDF word-level extraction with tolerance-based line clustering (tol=1.5) and fixed column X-bands over the table's 5 columns (Property number / Lot on plan / Street address / Place name / Listing). 283 of 283 rows extracted; 19 rows (6.7%) were corrupted by column-boundary drift between sub-table blocks (street-number digits bleeding into the lot/plan column), detected via a POSTCODE_RE regex quality gate and hand-corrected by visually reading zoomed crops of the specific source pages (1, 5, 13, 16, 17). Final dataset: 283 records, 0 remaining quality-gate failures.
cadastre_match_method: Each record's lot/plan text field (which may list multiple lot/plans per property, e.g. a building spanning several lots) was parsed into individual lotplan candidates via regex, then queried one at a time against the state cadastre (PlanningCadastre/LandParcelPropertyFramework/MapServer/4) until the first one resolved to a real parcel; that parcel is used to represent the whole property. 257 of 283 records (90.8%) resolved to a real cadastre parcel. The 26 unresolved are mostly Community Title / Building Units Plan common-property lots ("CP" lot number - a legal/registration construct with no independent cadastre polygon), a National Park (NPW) parcel, and a handful of plan-type prefixes (GTP - Group Titles Plan) not present in this cadastre layer - expected limitations, not extraction errors.
caveat: A hit (within 50m of one of the 257 matched lot/plans) is a reliable positive signal that the property is Schedule 7-listed (Local or State). A miss is NOT conclusive proof a property is unlisted - it may be one of the 26 unresolved records, or a transcription/matching gap. Always treat this as a supplementary heads-up, not an authoritative substitute for checking Schedule 7 directly for a specific address. The Listing column (Local/State) is preserved per-record but not currently exposed as a separate fact - all 257 matched places are surfaced under one generic 'near a Schedule 7 heritage place' site-constraint hit.
